composio.note: ServiceNow is listed under 'Bring your own OAuth app'; create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio lists ServiceNow among toolkits where you register your own OAuth app and supply its client ID and secret, so there is no managed app to borrow.

prerequisites.title: Admin role on a ServiceNow instance
prerequisites.detail: Managing OAuth needs the security_admin role. Other OAuth setup pages name oauth_admin or admin.

prerequisites.title: Valid (not self-signed) certificate
prerequisites.detail: ServiceNow OAuth does not support self-signed certificates on OAuth endpoints.

steps.title: Open Application Registry
steps.detail: Log in to the instance with an admin role and go to System OAuth > Application Registry.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client record
steps.detail: Create a new OAuth client record. The client ID is auto-generated; the client secret is shared between the instance and your app.
inputs: Redirect URI from the Composio dashboard
steps.done_when: A client ID and client secret exist.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config for the servicenow toolkit through Composio's API with your client ID and secret.

steps.title: Connect a test account
steps.detail: Authorize one user through Composio and check that the connection works. Re-authorize if you change refresh-token settings.

traps.title: Approval path is unconfirmed
traps.detail: The dossier found no statement on provider review, customer admin approval or limits before approval. Check before promising a launch date.

traps.title: Refresh token expiry setting
traps.detail: The Extend Refresh Token Expiry checkbox is in the provider configuration, and the connection must be re-authorized afterwards.

traps.title: Managed app limits do not apply
traps.detail: Managed apps share quota and enforce a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval; ServiceNow has no managed app, so use your own.

blockers.symptom: OAuth endpoint rejects the connection over certificate trust
blockers.what_it_means: The OAuth client does not allow endpoints using self-signed certificates.
blockers.what_to_do: Use a certificate from a trusted authority on the OAuth endpoint.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the certificate chain of the endpoint.

evidence.quote: Navigate to All > System OAuth > Application Registry.
evidence.answer: The first setup step is to open All > System OAuth > Application Registry in the ServiceNow console.

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: To create the OIDC entity, select New, then choose 'Configure an OIDC provider to verify ID tokens' and fill in the form. An existing template (ADFS, Auth0, Azure AD, Google, Okta) can also be selected instead.

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: The app must first be registered in the OpenID Connect provider before configuring the OAuth OIDC entity in ServiceNow.

evidence.answer: Each verifier map can point to a certificate record, and multiple verifier maps can be added for multiple keys.

evidence.answer: Custom JWT claims are added to the OAuth JWT Claim Validations related list. The iss, aud, sub and exp claims do not need records there.
